script:
export const meta = { name: 'md-spec-extract', description: 'Probe the Python markdown executable to extract exhaustive behavioral specs for a JS reimplementation', phases: [ { title: 'Probe', detail: '13 parallel domain probes writing spec files' }, { title: 'Gaps', detail: 'completeness critic over the written specs' }, ], } const D = '$' // dollar sign, used to keep template literals safe const HARNESS = ` ## Probe harness (already built, do not rewrite it) \`/tmp/probe/p.mjs\` is an ESM module exporting: - \`run({a,b,c,d,e,f})\` -> full stdout string (any omitted key defaults to a marker like 'MKAA') - \`phase(slot, text)\` -> the isolated output of one pipeline stage: - slot \`'a'\`,\`'b'\`,\`'c'\` => \`markdown.markdown(text)\` with NO extensions - slot \`'d'\` => \`extensions=['extra','tables']\` - slot \`'e'\` => \`extensions=['codehilite','fenced_code']\` - slot \`'f'\` => \`extensions=['toc']\` - slot \`'5'\` => phase5: \`extensions=['extra','tables','codehilite','fenced_code','toc']\`, \`output_format='xhtml'\` - \`phase5(text)\`, \`full(a,b,c,d,e,f)\` Write your own throwaway driver scripts under \`/tmp/work//\` that \`import { phase, run, full } from '/tmp/probe/p.mjs'\` and print \`JSON.stringify\` of every result so whitespace is unambiguous. Batch MANY cases per node process (each executable invocation costs ~0.5s; a batch of 60 cases in one node process is fine and takes ~30s). ## Rules - The ONLY source of truth is running \`/workspace/dataset/test19_executable\`. Never run \`python\`/\`python3\` (not available). - Never guess from memory of the Python libraries: every claim in your spec must be backed by an observed probe. Where you DO rely on library knowledge to pick what to probe, that is fine - but the recorded behavior must be observed. - You are producing a SPEC, not code. No implementation. ` const OUTPUT_RULES = (name) => ` ## Output Write your exhaustive findings to \`/tmp/specs/${name}.md\`. Requirements for that file: - Organised with headings; every rule stated precisely enough to implement without further probing. - Include a large "Observed cases" section: a list of \`INPUT (JSON-escaped)\` -> \`OUTPUT (JSON-escaped)\` pairs covering everything you probed, including the boring confirmations and every edge case. Aim for 60+ concrete cases. - Explicitly flag anything you could NOT determine, and anything surprising/counter-intuitive. - Be exhaustive: this file is the only thing the implementer will read. Length is not a concern; omissions are fatal. Then return (as your final message) a <=350 word summary: the top surprising/critical rules only. ` phase('Probe') const PROBES = [ { name: 'core-blocks', prompt: `Probe the CORE (no-extension) BLOCK-LEVEL markdown behavior of the executable, via slot 'a'. Cover exhaustively: - Whitespace normalisation: tabs (expand to 4? tabsize), CRLF and CR line endings, trailing whitespace on lines, leading blank lines, trailing newlines, a document of only whitespace, the empty string. - Paragraphs: joining of consecutive lines, blank-line separation, leading spaces (1,2,3,4+) on a paragraph line. - ATX headings: one to six hashes, seven hashes, missing space after #, closing hashes (\`## x ##\`), empty heading (\`#\`, \`##\` alone), leading spaces (1-3, 4). - Setext headings: \`=\` and \`-\` underlines, lengths 1..n, with trailing spaces, multi-line paragraph then underline, interaction with lists (\`- \` vs \`---\`). - Horizontal rules: \`***\`, \`---\`, \`___\`, with spaces \`* * *\`, \`- - -\`, minimum count, leading spaces, more than 3. - Unordered lists: markers \`*\`,\`+\`,\`-\`; mixed markers; tight vs loose (blank line between items) and the exact \`

\` wrapping rules; nested lists at 2,3,4,8 spaces of indent; lazy continuation lines; items containing blank lines; a list item containing an indented code block; list immediately after a paragraph (no blank line). - Ordered lists: any starting number, \`start\` attribute or not, \`)\` vs \`.\` delimiter, nesting, mixing ol/ul. - Blockquotes: \`>\` with and without space, nested \`> >\`, lazy continuation, blockquote containing list/heading/code, blank \`>\` lines. - Indented code blocks: 4 spaces / 1 tab, blank lines inside, trailing blank lines, exact trailing newline in output, HTML escaping inside. - Link reference definitions: \`[id]: url "title"\`, casing, indentation, multi-line, definitions removed from output. - Raw block-level HTML: \`

...
\`, \`

\`, self-closing, block tag list, inline tag at start of block, HTML with blank lines inside, markdown inside a raw HTML block (is it processed?), HTML comments, processing instructions, comments at top level, unclosed tags, script/style blocks. THIS IS CRITICAL: pipeline phase 3 feeds already-rendered HTML back into markdown, so nail the exact rules including the blank line that appears after each raw HTML block. - Ordering/interaction: heading immediately followed by list, etc. ${HARNESS}${OUTPUT_RULES('core-blocks')}`, }, { name: 'core-inline', prompt: `Probe the CORE (no-extension) INLINE markdown behavior of the executable, via slot 'a'. Wrap tests in a plain paragraph. Cover exhaustively: - Emphasis: \`*x*\`, \`_x_\`, \`**x**\`, \`__x__\`, \`***x***\`, \`____x____\`, intraword (\`a*b*c\`, \`a_b_c\`, snake_case_word), unmatched markers, nested emphasis, emphasis spanning newlines, emphasis with punctuation adjacency, \`**a*b*c**\`, \`*a**b**c*\`, whitespace right after the opening marker. - Code spans: single backtick, double backticks, spaces stripped?, backticks inside, unmatched backticks, HTML escaping inside code spans (less-than, ampersand, quote), markdown inside code spans, multi-line code spans. - Escapes: every ASCII punctuation preceded by a backslash - which are escapable, which stay literal; backslash before a letter; backslash at end of line (hard break?); double backslash. - Links: inline \`[t](url)\`, with title in single/double quotes, empty url \`[t]()\`, url in angle brackets, url containing spaces/parens/nested parens, title with quotes; reference links \`[t][id]\`, \`[t][]\`, \`[t]\` shortcut, case-insensitivity, missing reference; nested brackets in text; link text containing emphasis/code. - Images: \`![alt](src "title")\`, attribute ORDER in output, empty alt, reference images. - Autolinks: angle-bracket http/https/ftp/mailto URLs, bare emails like \`\` (note the character-reference obfuscation - document the EXACT algorithm: which characters become decimal \`&#NN;\` vs hex \`&#xNN;\`; probe many different email addresses to determine whether the choice is deterministic or random - RUN THE SAME INPUT 5+ TIMES to check stability). - Entities and special chars: bare ampersand, \`&\`, \`©\`, \`©\`, \`©\`, \`¬anentity;\`, less-than, greater-than, double quote, apostrophe in text; ampersand inside a link URL; less-than followed by a letter vs a space vs a digit. - Inline raw HTML: \`x\`, \`
\`, \`
\`, \`\`, attributes with markdown-ish content, unknown tags, \`<3\`, \`a < b\`. - Hard line breaks: two+ trailing spaces, one trailing space, backslash at EOL, a literally typed \`
\`. - Ampersand handling inside href and src. ${HARNESS}${OUTPUT_RULES('core-inline')}`, }, { name: 'ext-tables', prompt: `Probe the TABLES extension via slot 'd' (extensions=['extra','tables']) and cross-check slot '5'. Cover exhaustively: - Minimal valid table; with and without leading/trailing pipes; alignment rows \`:--\`, \`--:\`, \`:-:\`, \`-\`, \`---------\`; the exact \`style="text-align: X;"\` (or \`align=\`) attribute emitted and its exact spelling/spacing. - Column count mismatches: more cells in a body row than the header, fewer cells; empty cells; entirely empty rows. - Escaped pipes, pipes inside code spans, pipes inside inline HTML attributes. - Inline markdown inside cells (emphasis, code, links). - What makes a table INVALID and fall back to a paragraph (e.g. missing separator row, separator with wrong chars, only one line, separator not matching header column count). - Tables directly adjacent to other blocks (no blank line before/after), inside blockquotes, inside list items. - A table with only a header and separator (no body rows) - is \`\` emitted? - Multi-body / consecutive tables. - Exact whitespace/newlines in the emitted table markup (this must match character for character). - Also verify the behaviour under slot 'a' (no extension) so the fallback is documented. ${HARNESS}${OUTPUT_RULES('ext-tables')}`, }, { name: 'ext-fenced', prompt: `Probe the FENCED_CODE extension. Test it in slot 'd' (extra+tables => fenced_code WITHOUT codehilite) and slot 'e' (codehilite+fenced_code) and slot '5' (everything, xhtml). Cover exhaustively: - Fence characters: 3+ backticks, 3+ tildes; longer fences; mismatched open/close lengths; fence inside a fence. - Info string forms: backticks followed by \`python\`, by \` python\` (leading space), by \`{.python}\`, by \`{#id .python .foo key=val}\`, by \`python title="x"\`, by an unknown language, by nothing. - The exact emitted markup WITHOUT codehilite: \`

\` vs \`
\`; the exact class prefix; trailing newline before the closing code tag.
- HTML escaping inside fenced blocks: less-than, ampersand, greater-than, double quote, apostrophe.
- Unclosed fence at end of document.
- Blank lines inside the block; leading/trailing blank lines inside; the block's own indentation (fence indented by 1-3 spaces - is the indent stripped from content?).
- Fenced block inside a list item / blockquote.
- Interaction with the \`:::lang\` codehilite shebang syntax and a \`#!lang\` first line.
- Empty code block (fence, newline, fence).
- Whether the content is markdown-processed (it must not be) and whether raw-HTML postprocessing corrupts it.
- IMPORTANT: also probe what an INDENTED (4-space) code block produces under slot 'e' and slot '5' (does codehilite apply to it?).
${HARNESS}${OUTPUT_RULES('ext-fenced')}`,
  },
  {
    name: 'ext-toc',
    prompt: `Probe the TOC extension via slot 'f' (extensions=['toc']) and slot '5'.

The critical thing is the exact ID-generation (slugify) algorithm. Determine it precisely by probing:
- ASCII headings with spaces, mixed case, punctuation (period, comma, bang, question mark, colon, semicolon, apostrophe, quote, parens, brackets, slash, backslash, ampersand, at, hash, percent, plus, equals, star, tilde, backtick, angle brackets, pipe, dollar, caret), underscores, hyphens, digits, leading/trailing spaces, multiple internal spaces, tabs.
- NON-ASCII headings: Chinese (标题1, 这是一段文本), accented Latin (Café, naïve, Ünicode), Greek, Cyrillic, emoji, full-width digits/letters, ligatures, numero sign, one-half sign, combining marks. Hypothesis to CONFIRM OR REFUTE by probing: the value is Unicode NFKD-normalised, then non-ASCII characters are DROPPED, then non-word/non-space/non-hyphen chars removed, then trimmed, lowercased, and runs of whitespace collapsed to a hyphen. Probe enough cases to pin down the exact order and the exact character classes (in particular: is underscore kept? are digits kept? is an existing hyphen kept? what happens to a heading that slugifies to the EMPTY string?).
- Heading that slugifies to empty - what id is emitted? Probe several such headings in the SAME document to see the collision suffixes.
- Duplicate ids in one document: the exact suffix scheme (underscore-1? hyphen-1? starting at what number?), including duplicates of an already-suffixed id, and duplicates of an empty slug.
- Headings that already carry an id via attr_list (only relevant in slot '5' where attr_list is active through 'extra').
- The \`[TOC]\` marker: exact emitted markup (a div with class toc, nested lists, list items with anchors), nesting rules when heading levels skip, \`[TOC]\` inside a paragraph, multiple \`[TOC]\`, lowercase \`[toc]\`.
- Whether inline markdown in a heading is stripped for the id and for the TOC link text; what happens with an image or link inside a heading.
- Setext headings and ids.
- Confirm which slots DO and DO NOT add ids (slot 'a'/'d' should not).
${HARNESS}${OUTPUT_RULES('ext-toc')}`,
  },
  {
    name: 'ext-extra-misc',
    prompt: `Probe the remaining sub-extensions bundled in \`extra\` via slot 'd' (extensions=['extra','tables']) and slot '5'.
\`extra\` bundles: abbr, attr_list, def_list, fenced_code, footnotes, md_in_html, tables (fenced_code and tables are covered by other agents - focus on the rest).

Cover exhaustively:
- **abbr**: an abbreviation definition line plus usage; case sensitivity; multi-word abbreviations; abbreviation inside a word; abbr inside code; the exact \`\` markup; definition removed from output; definition anywhere in the doc.
- **attr_list**: \`{: #id .class key=val }\` and \`{ #id .class }\` on headings, paragraphs (trailing on last line), list items, block-level trailing, and inline forms on images and emphasis; attribute ORDER in emitted markup; multiple classes; quoted values; the dot/hash shorthand; invalid attr lists left literal.
- **def_list**: term then a colon-prefixed definition, multiple terms, multiple definitions, loose (blank line) vs tight definitions and the resulting paragraph wrapping, definition continuation lines, nested lists in definitions, exact dl/dt/dd whitespace.
- **footnotes**: a footnote reference plus its definition; the exact emitted markup (the sup element and its id, the footnote-ref anchor, the trailing footnote div, the horizontal rule, the ordered list, the backref anchor and its title and the return arrow entity) character for character; multiple footnotes and their ordering; multi-paragraph footnotes; undefined footnote reference; duplicate references to the same note; named (non-numeric) footnote labels.
- **md_in_html**: a div with \`markdown="1"\`, with \`markdown="block"\`, with \`markdown="span"\`, nested, and plain raw HTML with no markdown attribute; a raw HTML block that CONTAINS blank lines (critical: pipeline phase 3/4 feeds rendered HTML back in with blank lines inside). Compare slot 'a' vs slot 'd' vs slot '5' for the SAME raw-HTML input so the differences are explicit.
- Note which of these fire on the pipeline's own phase-3/phase-4 re-fed HTML.
${HARNESS}${OUTPUT_RULES('ext-extra-misc')}`,
  },
  {
    name: 'codehilite-behavior',
    prompt: `Probe the CODEHILITE extension's wrapper/dispatch behavior (NOT the individual language lexers - other agents do those).
Use slot 'e' (codehilite+fenced_code) and slot '5' (all extensions, xhtml).

Cover exhaustively:
- The exact wrapper markup: a div with class codehilite containing pre, an empty span, and code. Confirm the empty span, whether a class appears on the pre element, whether there is a trailing newline before the closing code tag, and whether the wrapper differs in slot '5' (xhtml).
- Language dispatch: which info-string languages produce highlighted output vs a plain unhighlighted block. Systematically test a LARGE list of language names and aliases and record, for each, whether it highlighted and what the first few spans were:
  python py python3 py3 javascript js node typescript ts jsx tsx html htm xhtml xml css scss sass less bash sh shell zsh console shell-session json json5 yaml yml toml ini sql java kotlin scala c cpp c++ csharp cs go rust rs ruby rb php perl swift objc r matlab lua dart haskell elixir erlang clojure groovy make cmake dockerfile nginx apache diff patch text plain plaintext txt markdown md rst latex tex graphql protobuf vim awk sed powershell ps1 batch bat asm
  (batch these ~70 probes efficiently; a tiny 1-line snippet per language is enough - just record whether spans appeared and the exact first 200 chars of output)
- Unknown / garbage language name: highlighted? what class?
- NO language given: is the language guessed? Test with content that strongly looks like python, like json, like HTML, like shell, and with prose text and with Chinese text. Determine whether guessing is enabled at all.
- The \`:::python\` first-line syntax and a \`#!/usr/bin/env python\` shebang first line, inside both fenced and 4-space-indented blocks.
- Indented (4-space) code blocks under codehilite: highlighted or not? what wrapper?
- Options in the info string: hl_lines, a brace-form with an id, linenos/linenums variants.
- Empty code block, code block that is only whitespace, code block with trailing blank lines, code containing a carriage return.
- Whether the language name appears anywhere in the output (a class on the div/pre/code).
- HTML escaping of less-than, greater-than, ampersand, double quote and apostrophe inside highlighted output (note \`'\` for apostrophes) and inside UNhighlighted output.
${HARNESS}${OUTPUT_RULES('codehilite-behavior')}`,
  },
  {
    name: 'pyg-python',
    prompt: `Reverse-engineer the PYTHON syntax highlighter's exact token stream. Probe with slot 'e', wrapping snippets in a
fenced block whose info string is \`python\`.

Your deliverable is a complete specification of the tokenizer: for every construct, the exact sequence of
(cssClass or none, text) spans produced. Note that adjacent tokens sharing a CSS class are MERGED into one span,
and tokens with no class are emitted as bare escaped text - so you must infer boundaries from cases where they differ.

Cover exhaustively (probe each in isolation AND in combination):
- Keywords (\`k\`): def class if elif else for while return yield import from as pass break continue with try except finally raise global nonlocal lambda assert del in is not and or async await; \`kn\` (import/from), \`kc\` (True False None), and which of in/is/not/and/or are \`ow\` vs \`k\`.
- Builtins (\`nb\`): print len range int str list dict set tuple open type isinstance super object Exception ValueError TypeError; \`bp\` for self/cls.
- Function/class definition names: \`nf\`, \`nc\`; decorators \`nd\`; the whitespace token after \`def\`/\`class\` (\`w\` vs plain).
- Names \`n\`, attribute access (is the attribute \`n\` or something else?), function CALLS (\`n\` or \`nf\`?), keyword arguments in a call, dunder names (\`fm\`?), module names after import (\`nn\`).
- Numbers: \`mi\` int, \`mf\` float, \`mh\` hex, \`mo\` octal, \`mb\` binary, exponents, complex, underscore separators.
- Strings: \`s1\` single, \`s2\` double, triple-quoted, docstrings (\`sd\`?), raw strings (\`sa\` prefix?), bytes, f-strings (probe an f-string with a braced expression carefully), escape sequences inside strings (\`se\`), percent formatting (\`si\`), adjacent string concatenation, unterminated strings.
- Comments \`c1\`, shebang (\`ch\`?), type comments.
- Operators \`o\`, punctuation \`p\`: which characters are which - equals, plus, minus, star, slash, double slash, percent, double star, comparisons, augmented assignment, at, arrow, colon, comma, semicolon, dot, parens, brackets, braces, pipe, ampersand, caret, tilde, shifts, walrus. Note the arrow and the colon in annotations.
- Whitespace: when is a space \`w\` (Whitespace) vs unclassed Text? Probe indentation, spaces around operators, the space after def/class/import/return, blank lines, tabs.
- Errors: \`err\` for invalid characters (dollar, question mark, backtick).
- Non-ASCII identifiers and Chinese text inside strings/comments.
- Line structure: a trailing newline is always present before the closing code tag; check how blank lines and the final line are emitted.
${HARNESS}${OUTPUT_RULES('pyg-python')}`,
  },
  {
    name: 'pyg-javascript',
    prompt: `Reverse-engineer the JAVASCRIPT syntax highlighter's exact token stream. Probe with slot 'e', wrapping snippets in a
fenced block whose info string is \`javascript\`.
Also check whether alias \`js\` behaves identically, and probe \`typescript\`/\`ts\` and \`jsx\` separately (record if they differ).

Adjacent tokens sharing a CSS class are MERGED into one span; unclassed tokens are bare escaped text.

Cover exhaustively:
- Keywords (\`k\`/\`kd\`/\`kr\`/\`kc\`): var let const function return if else for while do switch case break continue new delete typeof instanceof in of this class extends super import export from default async await yield try catch finally throw void with debugger; true false null undefined NaN Infinity; which get \`kd\`, which \`kr\`, which \`kc\`.
- Builtins (\`nb\`): Array Boolean Date Error Function JSON Math Number Object RegExp String console document window Promise Symbol Map Set - and which are \`nb\` vs \`nx\`.
- Identifiers \`nx\`; property access; function names in a function declaration (\`nf\`? \`nx\`?); class names; object literal keys; labels.
- Numbers: \`mi\`, \`mf\`, \`mh\`, \`mo\`, \`mb\`, exponents, BigInt, numeric separators.
- Strings: \`s1\` single, \`s2\` double, template literals (backtick) including interpolation, escapes (\`se\`), regex literals (\`sr\`) and how the lexer decides regex-vs-division (probe an assignment of a regex literal versus a chain of divisions).
- Comments: \`c1\` line, \`cm\` block, jsdoc.
- Operators \`o\` and punctuation \`p\`: assignment, equality, strict equality, relational, arithmetic, exponent, increment, logical, nullish, optional chaining, arrow, spread, bitwise, shifts, compound assignment, ternary, comma, semicolon, colon, dot, parens, brackets, braces. Determine which chars are \`o\` vs \`p\`.
- Whitespace: when is whitespace \`w\` vs unclassed? Probe indentation and spaces around operators.
- Errors \`err\` for invalid characters (hash, at-sign).
- Arrow functions, destructuring, spread, classes, generators, async/await, decorators.
- Non-ASCII/Chinese inside strings and comments.
${HARNESS}${OUTPUT_RULES('pyg-javascript')}`,
  },
  {
    name: 'pyg-html',
    prompt: `Reverse-engineer the HTML/XML/CSS/JSON/YAML syntax highlighters' exact token streams. Probe with slot 'e', wrapping
snippets in fenced blocks whose info strings are \`html\`, \`xml\`, \`css\`, \`scss\`, \`less\`, \`json\`, \`yaml\`.

Adjacent tokens sharing a CSS class are MERGED; unclassed tokens are bare escaped text.

For **html**, cover exhaustively:
- Tags: the angle brackets (class \`p\`), tag names (\`nt\`), closing tags, self-closing tags, uppercase tag names, unknown tags.
- Attributes: attribute names (\`na\`), the equals sign (\`o\`), quoted values (\`s\`), single vs double quotes, unquoted values, valueless attributes, attributes spanning lines.
- Text content: unclassed. Entities (\`ni\`?).
- Comments (\`c\`/\`cm\`?), doctype (\`cp\`? \`nt\`?), processing instructions, CDATA.
- Embedded style and script elements: is the content CSS-highlighted / JS-highlighted? Probe both, they are the trickiest part.
- Escaping: the emitted entity forms for each source character (less-than, greater-than, ampersand, apostrophe, double quote).
- Whitespace/indentation: \`w\` vs unclassed.
- Chinese text inside elements and attributes.

For **css**: selectors, braces, property names, colons, values, numbers with units, hex colors, strings, the important flag, comments, at-rules.
For **json**: keys, string values, numbers, true/false/null, punctuation, whitespace.
For **yaml** and **xml**: enough to implement the common cases.
${HARNESS}${OUTPUT_RULES('pyg-html')}`,
  },
  {
    name: 'pyg-bash',
    prompt: `Reverse-engineer the BASH/SHELL syntax highlighter's exact token stream. Probe with slot 'e', wrapping snippets in a
fenced block whose info string is \`bash\`.
Also check aliases \`sh\`, \`shell\`, \`zsh\`, \`console\`, \`shell-session\` and record whether they differ (console/shell-session use a different lexer - document it).

Adjacent tokens sharing a CSS class are MERGED; unclassed tokens are bare escaped text.
Known starting point (observed): the two-line script \`ls -la\` then \`echo ${D}PATH\` produces
\`ls -la\` newline \`echo ${D}PATH\` newline
So: \`ls\` is unclassed Text, the space is \`w\`, \`-la\` unclassed, \`echo\` is \`nb\` (builtin), \`${D}PATH\` is \`nv\`.

Cover exhaustively:
- Builtins \`nb\`: echo cd pwd export set unset read source alias eval exec exit return shift test printf let local declare typeset trap wait kill jobs history type hash umask ulimit getopts times readonly builtin command pushd popd dirs disown enable logout mapfile readarray suspend
  (probe a large list and record which get \`nb\`)
- Keywords \`k\`: if then else elif fi for while until do done case esac function in select time coproc.
- Variables \`nv\`: a bare dollar-name, a braced dollar-name, a braced name with a default, positional parameters, at-sign, star, question mark, double-dollar, hash, bang, zero, a plain assignment (is the LHS \`nv\`?), an exported assignment, an array subscript.
- Strings: double-quoted (\`s2\`) with variable interpolation inside (nested \`nv\`? \`si\`?), single-quoted (\`s1\`), dollar-single-quoted, escapes (\`se\`), heredocs (\`sh\`?).
- Comments \`c1\`, shebang (\`ch\`? \`c1\`?).
- Operators \`o\`: pipe, double pipe, double ampersand, semicolon, double semicolon, single ampersand, redirections, equals, comparisons, test operators; punctuation \`p\`: parens, braces, brackets.
- Command substitution with dollar-parens and with backticks, arithmetic expansion.
- Numbers, flags, paths, globs.
- Whitespace: when \`w\` vs unclassed (this seems to be a distinguishing feature of this lexer - pin it down precisely: is EVERY inter-token space \`w\`? what about leading indentation and newlines?).
- Chinese text in strings/comments/arguments.
${HARNESS}${OUTPUT_RULES('pyg-bash')}`,
  },
  {
    name: 'pyg-other',
    prompt: `Reverse-engineer the syntax highlighters for the REMAINING likely languages. Probe with slot 'e', wrapping snippets in
fenced blocks with the language as the info string. Another agent covers python / javascript / html+css+json+yaml+xml / bash - SKIP those.

Priority order (spend most effort on the first group, they are most likely to appear in tests):
1. \`text\`/\`plain\`/\`plaintext\`/\`txt\` and NO-language blocks: confirm what the plain/Text lexer emits (any spans at all? is whitespace \`w\`?).
2. \`java\`, \`c\`, \`cpp\`/\`c++\`, \`csharp\`/\`cs\`, \`go\`, \`rust\`/\`rs\`, \`ruby\`/\`rb\`, \`php\`, \`sql\`, \`typescript\`/\`ts\`.
3. \`ini\`, \`toml\`, \`diff\`, \`makefile\`/\`make\`, \`dockerfile\`, \`markdown\`/\`md\`, \`perl\`, \`swift\`, \`kotlin\`, \`lua\`, \`r\`, \`scala\`, \`powershell\`.

For each language: probe a representative ~8-line snippet exercising keywords, types, identifiers, function definitions,
strings, numbers, comments, operators and punctuation, and record the EXACT output. Then probe smaller isolated
constructs to pin down the token classes. Adjacent same-class tokens are MERGED; unclassed tokens are bare escaped text.

Also: for EVERY alias you test, record the canonical lexer it resolves to (by comparing outputs), and note aliases that
FAIL to resolve (unknown language => how is it rendered?).

Produce, for each language, a rule table precise enough to implement a tokenizer. If time forces a trade-off, prefer
depth on group 1 and 2 over breadth into group 3, but at minimum record one full example snippet output for every
language listed so an implementer can sanity check.
${HARNESS}${OUTPUT_RULES('pyg-other')}`,
  },
  {
    name: 'pipeline-and-cli',
    prompt: `Probe the PROGRAM-LEVEL behavior: argument parsing, the 9-phase pipeline, and the xhtml output format.
Use \`run()\`/\`full()\` from the harness and also invoke \`/workspace/dataset/test19_executable\` directly with \`execFileSync\`
so you can observe stderr and exit codes. Read \`/workspace/dataset/test19.py\` first - it is the source being reimplemented.

Cover exhaustively:
- **argparse**: missing a required arg (exact stderr text + exit code); unknown arg; \`-h\`/\`--help\` exact text + exit code;
  the \`--a=value\` form; \`--a\` with an empty value; prefix abbreviations; a value starting with a dash; the bare \`--\`
  separator; a repeated \`--a\` (last wins?); argument ORDER independence; a value containing newlines/unicode/quotes;
